title: The House After the House
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A fashion house may continue culturally after its operating company closes through objects, marks, debts, contracts, archives, people, methods, images, and contested memory—but none automatically stays together.
A less-remembered house remains researchable because its object record survives.

01 · CLOSE — What ended and when?. Record entity, business operation, employment, production, sales, licenses, domains, accounts, premises, and public announcement separately with authoritative dates.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · DISTRIBUTE — Where did assets and obligations go?. Track inventory, samples, cash, debt, contracts, marks, copyrights, data, domains, archives, equipment, and records by governing transaction and custodian.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · REMEMBER — Who preserves the history?. Map museums, archives, former workers, collaborators, customers, press, communities, and collectors with rights, privacy, correction, and provenance boundaries.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · NAME — How should later work describe continuity?. Distinguish revival, license, acquisition, homage, research, exhibition, successor, and unrelated reuse; attach the evidence for every relationship claim.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Create a dated closure map across operation, people, obligations, assets, and records.
Trace every claimed successor asset to a transaction or mark unresolved.
Invite former participants to correct the public chronology.
Review insolvency, corporate, labor, contract, IP, privacy, and tax issues with qualified professionals.
